title: Enterprise onboarding — support process, health checks, QBR and escalation playbook
author: Aisha Khatri
body:
Overview:

Purpose
This playbook consolidates the enterprise onboarding support process, integration checklist, escalation path, common known issues and workarounds, and a repeatable health check / QBR template. It is intended for Customer Success (CSE), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support Engineers, and Engineering on-call partners.

Scope
- Applies to all enterprise customers undergoing onboarding or ramping to production.
- Covers first 90 days of onboarding (kickoff -> integration -> production handoff) and recurrent quarterly health checks (QBRs).

Owner and stakeholders
- Document owner: Customer Success (Aisha Khatri)
- Primary stakeholders: Solutions Engineering, Support, Eng-SRE, Product
- SLAs and operational ownership listed in the Escalation matrix below.

Quick links
- Integration guide (detailed): /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-integration-playbook-2026
- Known issues index: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds
- Incident & SRE runbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks

Onboarding phases and checklist (90-day default)
1) Kickoff (Day 0–7)
   - Schedule 90-minute kickoff with CSE, SE, customer PM/Eng, and Security contact.
   - Share credentials and documentation: API keys (scoped), VPC peering details (if Private), test prompt set.
   - Deliverables: project brief, success metrics (latency, cost targets, availability), data handling matrix.

2) Integration (Day 7–30)
   - Tasks (SE + Customer):
     - Obtain example traffic profile (requests/sec, avg token length, peak windows).
     - Exchange TLS certs / network requirements for Private/Dedicated.
     - Implement SDK/HTTP client and run smoke test (see sample curl below).
     - Validate authentication, rate limit behavior, and error handling.
   - Smoke test sample (curl):
     curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \n       -H "Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_KEY}" \n       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n       -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-10b","input":"Hello world","max_tokens":32}'

3) Performance tuning & pre-prod validation (Day 30–60)
   - Baseline metrics collection: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, error rate, cost per 1k tokens.
   - Apply batching and cache settings recommended by Redwood Optimize; run A/B tests if needed.
   - Run regression prompt set (10–50 prompts) and capture quality deltas.

4) Production cutover & handoff (Day 60–90)
   - Canary plan: 1%, 10%, 100% rollout with success gates (latency, error rate, quality).
   - Finalize support contacts, escalation list, and runbook links.
   - Handoff doc: including final traffic profile, model/version, quantization profile, billing owner.

Integration checklist (minimum required items)
- API authentication and key rotation policy verified.
- Network connectivity: public API or Private VPC peering validated.
- Rate limit & quota plan in place.
- Observability integrations: metrics export (Prometheus / Datadog), tracing configured.
- Security review complete: data residency and PII handling documented.

Escalation matrix and process
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev 1 (Critical): Total production outage or >80% traffic failing, severe correctness regression causing material business impact. Target response: initial acknowledgement <= 15m, mitigation plan in 60m.
  - Sev 2 (High): Degraded performance (p95 latency > 2x SLA) or persistent errors for a subset of customers. Target acknowledgement <= 1h, mitigation plan in 4h.
  - Sev 3 (Medium): Functional bug, integration issue impacting limited customers or causing incorrect outputs without immediate business impact. Acknowledgement <= 4h, resolution or plan in 3 business days.
  - Sev 4 (Low): Minor issues, documentation requests, non-urgent feature requests. Response per normal support SLA.

Escalation steps (for on-call and CSE)
1) Triage in Support queue and reproduce with customer-provided artifact (trace ID, request sample, timestamps).
2) Attach logs/traces and initial hypothesis; assign severity.
3) For Sev1/2: page Eng-SRE and Serving Runtime on-call (use PagerDuty group: Redwood-Serving-Prod).
4) If cause is model-quality, page Applied ML / Model Onboarding team; for infra capacity, page Cloud-Fleet.
5) Communicate every 30 minutes until mitigation for Sev1; hourly for Sev2.
6) After mitigation, run post-incident checklist and document RCA in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems.

Contact table (primary -> secondary)
- Customer Success (CSE): primary CSE -> backup CSE
- Support Engineers: support@redwood.dev -> se-oncall@redwood.dev
- Eng-SRE on-call: paged via PagerDuty -> eng-sre-rotation@redwood.dev
- Applied ML / Model Onboarding: model-onboard@redwood.dev -> am-rotation@redwood.dev

Known issues and common workarounds (summary table)
| Symptom | Probable cause | Workaround / Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| 429 Rate limit errors during burst | Client not handling 429; no retry/backoff | Implement exponential backoff, client-side queueing, request deduplication; request quota increase for Dedicated customers |
| Elevated p95 latency on long sequences | KV-cache misses + large context | Recommend model variant with KV-friendly quantization; enable prefix caching; reduce context window or route to high-memory pool |
| Model hallucination on domain terms | Missing domain-adaptive prompts | Add domain-specific system prompt, provide few-shot examples, or use reranking pipeline with ground-truth check |
| Intermittent TLS handshake failures (Private) | MTU/path or cert chain mismatch | Verify MTU/path MTU, re-issue certs with full chain, restart edge proxy |

Support process and SLAs
- Support tiers: Standard (email & portal, 24–48h response), Priority (1h/4h targets for Sev2/Sev1 during business hours), Enterprise (24/7 with committed PD escalation and quarterly QBR).
- Escalation timelines are contractual; verify customer contract for any custom SLA.

Health checks and QBR template
Use this template during monthly health checks (first 90 days) and quarterly QBRs afterwards.
Sections to include:
- Executive summary: 1 paragraph on overall health and top risks.
- Usage summary: traffic profile, tokens/day, peak concurrency, cost per 1k tokens.
- Reliability: uptime, error rate (30d), p95 latency (30d), incidents since last QBR.
- Quality: example prompts, baseline vs current model quality deltas, known regressions.
- Optimization opportunities: batching improvements, cache hits, model swap recommendations.
- Action items & owners: clear owners, due dates, and impact estimates.

QBR sample metrics table (30d window)
- Uptime: 99.95%
- Error rate (5xx): 0.12%
- Latency p50/p95: 85ms / 420ms
- Cost per 1k tokens: $0.56
- Model quality regression: 0.8% on acceptance test set

Postmortem & continuous improvement
- For Sev1/2 incidents, produce a written RCA within 7 days. Include timeline, root cause, mitigation, and long-term fix.
- Feed regressions into Applied ML regression triage and release gated rollouts.

Templates and artifacts (copy & fill)
- Pre-prod checklist (table format)
- Network runbook snippet (example commands and ports)
- QBR slide deck template (link to shared drive)

Appendix: useful commands and traces
- Retrieve request traces (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_KEY}" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/trace/${TRACE_ID}
- Example JSON log lines to attach: {"request_id": "abc-123", "model": "rwd-llm-10b", "latency_ms": 512}
